questions.question: What lane space are motorcycles entitled to use?

options.text: The bicycle lane.
The same full lane width as other motor vehicles.
Half the width of a lane.
The width of the sidewalk.

questions.correctAnswerText: The same full lane width as other motor vehicles.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles are entitled to use the same full lane width as all other vehicles.

questions.question: What should you do when you see a flashing yellow light at an intersection?

options.text: Slow down and proceed with care.
Continue normally through the intersection.
Stop and wait for a green light.
Stop and proceed when the way is clear.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and proceed with care.
questions.explanation: A flashing yellow light means caution. Slow down, look both ways, and proceed carefully.

questions.question: When may you pass another vehicle?

options.text: On a hill or curve because oncoming traffic is unlikely.
By driving on the shoulder of the highway.
By crossing a solid yellow line when the passing lane is clear.
None of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: None of the above.
questions.explanation: Do not pass on hills or curves because you cannot see oncoming traffic. Never drive on the shoulder to pass. Never cross a solid yellow line to pass.

questions.question: When can you drive through an intersection if the light turns yellow?

options.text: If an emergency vehicle is crossing.
If pedestrians are crossing.
If you are turning right.
If you were already in the intersection when the light turned yellow.

questions.correctAnswerText: If you were already in the intersection when the light turned yellow.
questions.explanation: If you are already in the intersection when the light turns yellow, you may continue through carefully.

questions.question: You hear a siren but cannot see an emergency vehicle yet. What should you do?

options.text: Keep driving until you see the vehicle.
Pull to the curb and look to see which direction it is coming from.
Slow down but do not stop until you see it.
Speed up and turn at the next corner.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull to the curb and look to see which direction it is coming from.
questions.explanation: Pull safely to the right side of the road and stop. Look to see if the emergency vehicle is on your street before proceeding.

questions.question: What does a solid yellow line on your side of the centerline mean?

options.text: Slow down.
Pass with caution.
Do not pass.
Keep right on hills.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not pass.
questions.explanation: A solid yellow line next to your lane means you cannot pass vehicles in the other direction.

questions.question: What should you do when approaching a railroad crossing?

options.text: Slow down.
Look for a train.
Be ready to stop.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Slow down, look for a train, and be ready to stop. If red lights are flashing or a gate is down, stop 15 to 50 feet before the tracks. Do not try to go around the gate.

questions.question: When can you drive across a dashed white line?

options.text: At any time.
Only during daylight hours.
When it is safe to change lanes.
Only when passing a motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: When it is safe to change lanes.
questions.explanation: Dashed white lines separate lanes moving in the same direction. You may cross them to change lanes when it is safe to do so.

questions.question: What does an "End school zone" sign mean?

options.text: The speed limit is 20 mph.
A reduced speed zone is beginning.
You should expect pedestrians.
The reduced speed zone has ended.

questions.correctAnswerText: The reduced speed zone has ended.
questions.explanation: An "End school zone" sign marks where the reduced speed school zone ends. You can resume normal speed after this sign.

questions.question: Your wheels drop off the pavement onto the shoulder. What should you do?

options.text: Brake hard and turn sharply back onto the pavement.
Stop your car on the edge of the road.
Slow down and carefully turn back onto the pavement.
Keep your speed and turn sharply back onto the pavement.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and carefully turn back onto the pavement.
questions.explanation: Reduce your speed without braking and carefully turn back onto the pavement. Watch for nearby traffic as you re-enter the road.

questions.question: You see a sign that says "Reduced speed, 35 mph." What does this mean?

options.text: The new 35 mph speed limit starts at this sign.
The new 35 mph speed limit starts at the next speed limit sign.
You have plenty of time to slow down before the reduced speed zone.
You should reduce your speed to 35 mph only when the weather is bad.

questions.correctAnswerText: The new 35 mph speed limit starts at this sign.
questions.explanation: "Reduced speed" signs tell drivers to reduce their speed. The new speed limit begins right at the sign.

questions.question: After stopping for a school bus that is unloading children, what should you do?

options.text: Do not go until the children wave at you.
Watch for children walking along the side of the road.
Speed up quickly.
Turn on your hazard lights.

questions.correctAnswerText: Watch for children walking along the side of the road.
questions.explanation: After stopping for a school bus, watch for children walking along the side of the road. Always drive carefully around children.

questions.question: When can you cross double solid yellow lines?

options.text: To pass a slow truck.
To turn into a driveway.
To pass another car.
Never.

questions.correctAnswerText: To turn into a driveway.
questions.explanation: Double solid lines mean you cannot pass or change lanes. You can only cross them to turn left into a driveway, enter or exit a highway, or make a legal U-turn.

questions.question: When can you NOT cross a single broken white or yellow line?

options.text: When it would interfere with other traffic.
When turning left into a driveway.
When the car in front of you has broken down.
When passing on the right on a one-way street.

questions.correctAnswerText: When it would interfere with other traffic.
questions.explanation: You can cross a single broken line to pass or change lanes if you can do so safely and without interfering with traffic.

questions.question: How can you avoid making emergency stops while driving in traffic?

options.text: Honk your horn to let others know you are there.
Look ahead and keep a safe distance from other cars.
Drive in the right lane only.
Drive slower than the flow of traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look ahead and keep a safe distance from other cars.
questions.explanation: A safe following distance lets you react to problems without emergency stops, which could cause the car behind you to crash into you.

questions.question: What do orange signs mean?

options.text: Work zone warning.
Rules and regulations.
School zone.
Directions and information.

questions.correctAnswerText: Work zone warning.
questions.explanation: Orange signs are used in work zones. They are usually diamond-shaped with black letters or symbols. They warn that workers are on or near the road.

questions.question: If an oncoming car is heading toward you in your lane, what should you do?

options.text: Honk, steer right, and speed up.
Honk, steer left, and brake.
Honk, steer right, and brake.
Stay in your lane, honk, and brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Honk, steer right, and brake.
questions.explanation: If a car is coming at you head-on, honk to get the driver's attention. If they do not move, steer right. If you steer left and they correct at the last second, you will still crash. Brake hard and steady. Every mile per hour slower reduces the crash impact.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Lane ends.
No right turn.
Road is slippery when wet.
Two-way traffic ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Lane ends.
questions.explanation: Warning signs prepare drivers for upcoming road conditions and hazards. They are yellow and black. This sign tells you a lane is ending and you should be ready for traffic to merge safely.

questions.question: What should you NOT do when changing lanes?

options.text: Check your side and rearview mirrors.
Use your turn signal.
Check for other drivers moving into the same lane.
Use your cell phone to call the police to check if the road is clear.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use your cell phone to call the police to check if the road is clear.
questions.explanation: Before changing lanes, check your mirrors for traffic behind you. Use your turn signal to alert other drivers. Check for other drivers who may be moving into the same lane.

questions.question: When driving on an interstate, what should you do?

options.text: Stop on the shoulder if you are tired.
Always use cruise control.
Signal, check mirrors, and check blind spots before changing lanes.
Change lanes frequently.

questions.correctAnswerText: Signal, check mirrors, and check blind spots before changing lanes.
questions.explanation: Signal, check your mirrors, and check your blind spot before changing lanes or passing on an interstate. Only stop on the shoulder in an emergency. Change lanes as little as possible. Do not use cruise control in heavy traffic or bad weather.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Road construction ahead.
The road curves left, then right.
The road curves right, then left.
Steep hill ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: The road curves right, then left.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that the road will curve to the right and then to the left. Slow down so you can safely turn through these curves.

questions.question: If a crossing guard is directing traffic in a school zone, you must:

options.text: Follow the crossing guard's directions.
Follow other drivers instead of the crossing guard.
Assume the guard should not be there.
Drive as if no children are present.

questions.correctAnswerText: Follow the crossing guard's directions.
questions.explanation: Always obey a crossing guard's directions. Slow down and use extra caution in school zones.

questions.question: When passing a large vehicle, the driver of a small vehicle must be prepared for:

options.text: Loud noises.
Excess air pollution.
Strong wind gusts from the large vehicle.
Falling vehicle parts.

questions.correctAnswerText: Strong wind gusts from the large vehicle.
questions.explanation: Large vehicles create strong wind gusts that can push smaller vehicles sideways. Be ready to steer to stay in your lane when passing or being passed by large vehicles.

questions.question: What should you do when entering a roadway from a private road?

options.text: Honk your horn to warn other cars.
Partially block the roadway to alert drivers.
Drive out quickly to merge with traffic.
Yield to pedestrians and roadway traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yield to pedestrians and roadway traffic.
questions.explanation: When leaving a private road or driveway, you must let pedestrians and traffic on the main road go first.

questions.question: What kinds of drugs can affect your driving ability?

options.text: Allergy medicine
Marijuana
Cold medicine
All of these

questions.correctAnswerText: All of these
questions.explanation: Many drugs can harm your driving ability. This includes illegal drugs and legal prescription or over-the-counter medicines. Driving while impaired by any drug is a crime.

questions.question: Allow extra space when stopping:

options.text: On a hill going upward.
At an intersection.
At a stop sign.
At a toll plaza.

questions.correctAnswerText: On a hill going upward.
questions.explanation: Leave more space in front of your vehicle when stopped on an uphill slope. If the vehicle ahead rolls backward, extra space helps prevent a crash.

questions.question: To help prevent crashes, you should:

options.text: Signal and communicate with other road users.
Ignore what other drivers do.
Drive only on small streets and back roads.
Avoid driving during busy hours.

questions.correctAnswerText: Signal and communicate with other road users.
questions.explanation: Many crashes happen because drivers surprise each other. Signal when you slow down, stop, or turn. Use your horn when needed. This helps drivers, cyclists, and pedestrians know what you are doing.

questions.question: A "No standing" sign means:

options.text: You can never stop your vehicle there.
You can park there with the driver inside.
You can stop briefly to pick up or drop off passengers.
You can stop to load or unload goods.

questions.correctAnswerText: You can stop briefly to pick up or drop off passengers.
questions.explanation: A "No standing" sign allows you to make a short stop only to pick up or drop off passengers.

questions.question: You hear a siren behind you while driving. You should:

options.text: Stop where you are.
Pull to the right and stop.
Speed up to get out of the way.
Slow down.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull to the right and stop.
questions.explanation: When you hear a siren or see flashing lights behind you, slow down and move to the right side of the road. Stop to let the emergency vehicle pass. If traffic is heavy and you are directly in front of the emergency vehicle, keep moving slowly until you can safely get out of the way.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: School ahead.
School crossing.
Pedestrian crossing.
Construction workers on or near the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pedestrian crossing.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are diamond-shaped with black symbols on a yellow background. They alert drivers to hazards ahead. This sign warns that people may be crossing the road.
